advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate/parse `ts` in `write_snapshot` (e.g. call `_to_naive_utc(ts)`) so an unparseable timestamp fails loud at write time instead of being silently dropped on every read.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/snapshot.py:45: `line = json.dumps({"ts": ts, "record": record}, sort_keys=True)` — `ts` is stored verbatim, never validated
ABSENCE: no `_to_naive_utc(ts)` call in write_snapshot to reject an invalid timestamp at write time
advisory.finding: `write_snapshot` accepts and persists `ts` without ever parsing it, but `read_snapshots` silently skips any line whose `ts` fails `_to_naive_utc` (the except catches ValueError). A caller passing a malformed/non-ISO `ts` gets a successful write that is then invisible on every read forever — silent, permanent data loss with no signal at write time.
advisory.suggested_fix: In write_snapshot, call `_to_naive_utc(ts)` before appending so an invalid ts raises ValueError to the caller rather than producing an unreadable record.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify/handle date-only `until`: either document that a date-only upper bound means midnight (excludes same-day-after-00:00) or extend it to end-of-day.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/snapshot.py:59: `high = _to_naive_utc(until)` — date-only 'until' becomes 00:00:00 of that day
advisory.finding: Date-only `until` bounds are parsed to midnight (00:00:00) and comparison is inclusive on the exact timestamp, so a record stamped later on the same day as `until` (e.g. ts `2026-06-01T12:00:00` with `until="2026-06-01"`) is excluded — a likely-surprising 'through end-of-day' expectation for a date-only upper bound.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting a snapshot whose timestamp equals `since` (and one equal to `until`) is returned, pinning the inclusive closed-range contract.
evidence: snapshot.py:72 `if low <= stamp <= high:` and docstring snapshot.py:6-7 promise an 'inclusive `[since, until]` range'
test_snapshot.py round-trip uses ts=2026-03-15 with range 2026-01-01..2026-06-01 — strictly interior, never on a bound
test_snapshot_heldout.py test_append_accumulates and test_malformed_line_skipped also use only interior timestamps (2026-02-01/02 within 2026-01-01..2026-03-01)
ABSENCE: no assertion where stamp == since or stamp == until, so the closed-vs-half-open boundary is not pinned
advisory.finding: The closed-range boundary inclusivity contract ([since, until] inclusive, implemented as `low <= stamp <= high`) is never tested at the exact bounds: no test uses a record whose timestamp equals `since` or `until`, so a regression flipping either `<=` to `<` would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor changes `low <= stamp <= high` to a half-open comparison, silently dropping records taken exactly at the query boundary
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test writing a record at ts='2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00' and asserting it is returned by read_snapshots('2026-03-15', '2026-03-15', ...) (and by ranges whose since or until equals that stamp).
